allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 33 m tall and 45 cm across at breast height at 60 years in a closed stand. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: soft dark green needles with paler undersides; dark reddish-brown furrowed bark. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): flat needles of mixed lengths, 0.5 to 2 cm long and 1.5 to 2 mm wide, so a needle 0.12 as wide as it is long (`width`), and needles about 1.2 cm on a spray 25 cm long (`needle` 0.047), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): thin dark reddish-brown bark furrowed into flat ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle`, `ranks` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated needles.

appearance.organs.spray.shape.needle.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

appearance.organs.spray.shape.ranks.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall, narrow conifer with a drooping leader, slender level to drooping branches and feathery, flat sprays of short needles in two ranks; very shade tolerant. Not fitted to measurements. Cones (plant forms F3): 1.5 to 3 cm hang from the shoot tips; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spray area (plant roadmap P4): the area its card draws with needles of their true length. Spec rework E6d: `cone_length`, `cone_pitch` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe, and `pipe_rings` refitted to the dbh references now that the crown holds more foliage.

generator.params.adult_age.note: The juvenile period is the time from germination to the first flowers, cones or seed, which the Woody Plant Seed Manual's tables give as the minimum seed-bearing age (spec rework P6). adult_age is the first year a program measuring it by the plant's age lets the plant flower or bear cones, so it is the juvenile period itself.

generator.params.cone_length.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

generator.params.cone_pitch.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): the sexual system its taxa state most often decides; a species whose taxa state dioecy no more often than another system bears both sexes on every plant until it states its own.

generator.params.height_max.note: What the conifer and succulent programs' height_max means: the height their Chapman-Richards curve rises toward with age and never reaches, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest ("trees to 40 m"). Plants of a usual age stand below it, as the curve says. Where a flora's greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.params.wood_density.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

generator.program.note: The conifers' own program (growth plan G2.3a), renamed from `conifer` and homed here: a leader laying down whorls of branches each year, with sprays of foliage and cones.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
